source.filename: A4-2021-Nonlinear vibration isolation via a nitinol wire rope.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Wire rope is cut in the middle into two segments, each initially modeled as a cantilever beam with constant cross-section clamped at the base and guided at the payload without rotation (rotation angle theta_w = 0).
Restoring force due to linear elastic deformation and geometric constraints follows a two-dimensional beam constraint model under initial axial tension.
Inner friction and NiTiNOL material phase transition effects are modeled phenomenologically via a modified Bouc-Wen model augmented with an exponential pinching effect function.
Payload motion is restricted strictly to vertical translation via a linear bearing on a vertical guiding rod.
Base excitation is assumed to be purely harmonic vertical displacement Yb = Ab * cos(wb * T).
Total restoring force of the wire rope is assumed to be an odd symmetric function of displacement, producing only odd harmonic responses.
Harmonics higher than the third order are assumed negligible for relative displacement amplitudes a < 3.
Hysteretic damping induced by internal friction and phase transitions is assumed to be rate-independent (independent of frequency).
control_variables: Payload mass M (6.46 kg in validation comparison)
Wire rope beam geometric and physical parameters: length L, cross-sectional area A, moment of inertia I, Young's modulus E, initial axial tension Fwx0
Nominal Bouc-Wen and pinching parameters: Kw1 = 2.17 N/mm, Kw3 = 0.53 N/mm^3, Kd = 217 N/mm, xi = 0.9, Yb = 215.57 mm^2, G = 0.591 mm^-1, B = 0.501 mm^-1, nb = 1
Initial equilibrium state where moving part gravity is fully balanced by the vertical linear spring with horizontal wire rope alignment
dependent_variables: Total restoring force Fr and dimensionless restoring force fr
Anhysteretic restoring force fan and anhysteretic force variable zan
Generalized equivalent stiffness Ke and dimensionless equivalent stiffness ke
Resonant frequency and dimensionless resonant frequency eta_r
Peak displacement transmissibility Tp and minimum peak transmissibility Tpmin
Most suitable excitation amplitudes Ab-pmin and Ab-rmin
Nonlinear jump phenomena branches (stable and unstable solutions)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: The restoring force of a NiTiNOL wire rope can be formulated by combining a physical beam constraint model for elastic geometric stiffness and a modified Bouc-Wen model with an exponential function for pinched hysteretic damping.

The generalized equivalent stiffness displays a stiffness-softening-hardening profile, where initial stiffness is primarily governed by the pinching parameter xi, small-displacement softening by Bouc-Wen sum (beta + gamma), and large-displacement hardening by cubic stiffness k3.

The rate-independent generalized equivalent damping ratio varies non-monotonically, first increasing and then decreasing with displacement amplitude due to the combined Bouc-Wen hysteresis and pinching effect.

Compared to an isolator with a steel wire rope, the NiTiNOL wire rope isolator possesses lower initial stiffness and higher equivalent damping, preventing unbounded resonant responses and providing superior broadband vibration isolation.

Both peak displacement transmissibility and resonant frequency vary non-monotonically with excitation amplitude, defining optimal excitation amplitudes for resonance suppression (Ab-pmin) and for low-frequency isolation (Ab-rmin).

Harmonic balance method using alternating frequency/time domain formulation closely matches Runge-Kutta numerical integration for the modified Bouc-Wen model, although third-order truncation excludes superharmonic resonances.

Analytical predictions show general agreement with experimental swept-frequency acceleration response data from a NiTiNOL wire rope damper, though both the analytical model and Runge-Kutta numerical integration fail to reproduce the experimentally observed softening at 7.68 m/s^2.

experimental_setup: No primary experimental apparatus was built or tested by the authors in this study.

For model verification, secondary experimental data from previously published literature (Carboni and Lacarbonara, 2016) was used, involving swept-frequency base acceleration tests (at 6.35 m/s^2 and 7.68 m/s^2) on a damper comprising horizontal symmetric NiTiNOL wire ropes without a vertical spring.
independent_variables: Base excitation frequency wb (dimensionless frequency ratio eta)
Bouc-Wen model parameters: Kd, G, B, nb (dimensionless beta, gamma, beta/gamma, beta + gamma)
Pinching effect parameters: xi and Yb (dimensionless yb)
limitations_inferred: No physical experimental testing was conducted on the complete proposed isolator prototype (wire rope combined with the vertical linear spring and linear bearing); validation relied solely on third-party damper data.
One-dimensional vertical motion is assumed with an idealized frictionless bearing, ignoring real-world friction, guiding rod misalignment, off-axis rotation, and multi-axis vibrations.
Thermomechanical coupling, ambient temperature dependence, and strain-rate sensitivity of NiTiNOL pseudoelastic phase transitions are omitted from the rate-independent phenomenological model.
Fatigue life, degradation of shape memory effect, and long-term shakedown behavior under large cyclic deformation were not evaluated.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The harmonic balance analysis failed to capture superharmonic resonances (at approximately fb = 2.4 Hz) observed in numerical integration due to truncation of harmonics beyond the third order.
Both the proposed harmonic balance method and direct Runge-Kutta numerical integration failed to characterize the stiffness-softening phenomenon observed in experimental results at Ub = 7.68 m/s^2.
The third-order harmonic approximation assumes higher-order harmonics are negligible, which is valid only when relative response amplitude is not too high (a < 3).
main_results: The proposed NiTiNOL wire rope isolator displays a stiffness-softening-hardening response and a rate-independent equivalent damping ratio that non-monotonically increases then decreases with displacement amplitude.

Pinching parameter xi primarily governs the initial equivalent stiffness, Bouc-Wen parameter sum (beta + gamma) controls small-displacement softening, and cubic stiffness k3 dictates large-displacement hardening.

The NiTiNOL wire rope achieves higher energy dissipation and lower initial stiffness than a steel wire rope, successfully mitigating resonance without the unbounded response observed in the steel wire rope system at Ab = 1 mm.

Peak displacement transmissibility and resonant frequency both exhibit non-monotonic relationships with excitation amplitude; for baseline parameters, the optimal excitation amplitude for minimum peak transmissibility is Ab-pmin = 1.08 mm (Tpmin = 2.65) and for lowest resonant frequency is Ab-rmin = 1.00 mm (eta_rmin = 0.25).

Depending on the parameter combinations, the isolator can exhibit either stiffness-softening jump phenomena (resonance peak bent to the left) or stiffness-hardening jump phenomena (resonance peak bent to the right).
Harmonic balance analysis with an alternating frequency/time domain technique demonstrates strong agreement with direct Runge-Kutta numerical integration and secondary experimental data.
modeling_methods: Beam constraint model (two-dimensional beam flexure under initial axial tension)
Modified Bouc-Wen phenomenological model with an exponential pinching effect function
Harmonic balance method (HBM) with first- and third-order harmonics
performance_metrics: Displacement transmissibility TD (dimensionless payload response amplitude ap = Ap / Ab)
Peak displacement transmissibility Tp and minimum peak transmissibility Tpmin
Resonant frequency and minimum resonant frequency eta_rmin
Most suitable excitation amplitude for resonance suppression (Ab-pmin) and for low-frequency vibration isolation (Ab-rmin)
possible_gap_implications: While NiTiNOL wire ropes offer passive variable stiffness and hysteretic damping for vibration isolation, translating these elements into soft robotics, continuum robots, or soft grippers would require addressing multi-axis loading, active thermal/electrical phase transition control, and bidirectional compliance rather than purely passive harmonic isolation.
paper.research_objective: To propose and analyze a nonlinear vibration isolator incorporating a horizontal NiTiNOL wire rope and a vertical linear spring; develop a restoring force model combining a beam constraint model and a modified Bouc-Wen model with pinching effects; solve the nonlinear dynamics using a harmonic balance method with an alternating frequency/time domain technique; and investigate the non-monotonic stiffness, damping, transmissibility, and optimal excitation amplitudes.
paper.research_problem: Conventional vibration isolators often struggle with trade-offs between low-frequency isolation and payload capacity; existing nonlinear damping mechanisms rely on complex geometric arrangements and are predominantly viscous; wire rope isolators with ring geometry present unfavorable asymmetric restoring forces; and non-monotonic variations in stiffness and damping introduce non-monotonic frequency responses requiring identification of optimal excitation amplitudes.
stiffness_mechanism: NiTiNOL wire rope under geometric constraints (beam flexure under tension)
pseudoelastic phase transitions and pinching effect of NiTiNOL
paper.title: Nonlinear Vibration Isolation via a NiTiNOL Wire Rope
